note: Phase 4: what the townsfolk say, chosen by conditions: intro (the first time), season, weather (rain covers storms), time (morning before 12:00, afternoon, evening from 18:00), event (something done in the park: site:<id>, milestone:<id>, badger, jobs:<count>) and min_hearts. No line repeats within a week for the same person. 4a first pass: about a dozen lines each.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: You're the new ranger! Sit, sit. First cup's on the house. Every cup's sort of on the house if you look sad enough.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: Morning. I've been up since four. Don't tell anyone, they'll think something's wrong.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: Rain's good for business. Nobody wants to be anywhere but here.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: The trick to a good espresso is to stop thinking about it right before it's ready.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: Agnes takes hers with three sugars and pretends it's one. I pretend I don't see.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: You smell like pine needles. It's a good look for a ranger.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: Snow day. I put cinnamon in everything until the thaw. Everything.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: Spring muffins are rhubarb. If you don't like rhubarb, I'll fight you, politely.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: Late? I'm always here late. Well. Here or somewhere near here.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: Someone said the old cabin has its door back on. Was that you? It was you.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: Visitors in the park! Two of them came in for coffee and asked if the woods were always like that. I said, like what?

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: You've been busy out there. You've got that look. I'll make it a double.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: You know, most people order and leave. You stay and talk. I like that.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: Some mornings this place is so quiet I can hear the milk steamer thinking.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: You're the ranger. Too thin. Sit down, I'm bringing you something. No, you don't get a choice.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: Teo is in the kitchen being quiet. He's always quiet. I'm loud enough for both of us.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: Mondays I close. Even a cook has to sit down once a week. Teo says twice. Teo is wrong.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: Rain! Good. Pozole weather. Everybody comes in wet and leaves warm.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: In this town nothing happens. I tell you, it's the best thing about it.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: You eat out there in the woods? What do you eat? Beans from a tin? Ay. Come here more.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: Summer, I put chiles on everything. If you cry, it's working.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: Evening. The good tables are by the window. Sit anywhere, I'll move you.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: The pond is open again? Teo used to fish there when he was small. Caught nothing. Very happy.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: There's a badger causing trouble out there, I hear. Bring it here. I'll feed it. It'll calm down.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: You come back. That's the main thing. You always come back.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: You know what this town needed? Somebody to cook for. Now I have you.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: Oh. Hi. You're the ranger. Mom told me to say hello. Hello.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: I'm not really a cook. I'm someone who's cooking. There's a difference.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: Sometimes the bins out back make a sort of rhythm when the wind's up. Never mind.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: The library has a book of old songs. I've read it eleven times. Not for any reason.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: Spring makes everyone in town hum. Haven't you noticed?

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: It's raining. Good. Nobody can hear anything but rain.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: Late shift. I like the town at night. Everything sounds further away.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: You fixed the tower road? I always wanted to see the tower up close. I mean, from a distance. Closer distance.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: People talk about the park like it's a story. You actually go in it. That's brave.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: You're easy to talk to. I don't say that to people. I don't say a lot of things to people.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: I wrote something new. A few bars. Maybe one day I'll let somebody hear it.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Ranger. Good. About time the park had one. Boots off the mat, please, I just swept.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Layers. Always layers. The mountain doesn't care how you feel about it.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Nell's restless again. She gets it from me. Don't tell her that.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Sundays I close. I hike. Slowly. At my age the view comes to you.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Winter out there will eat you if you let it. Buy a proper coat. I'll sell you one.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Rain shell. You need a rain shell. I'm not selling, I'm advising. Also selling.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Morning. Coffee? No. Wren's coffee? Fine.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Heard you made it to the outlook. Good. Some people only look at maps.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Found a lost party, did you? Good ranger work. Quietly done. That's how it should be.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: You're doing all right. I don't say that often. Don't make me say it twice.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: I had a ranger's patch once. Long time ago. Lent it to someone. Never got it back. Never minded.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: You're the ranger? Lucky. You get to go in every day. I've been meaning to for years.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: Mom thinks I'm going to leave town. I think she might be right. I don't know.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: Some mornings I walk to the gate and just look down the road. Then I come to work.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: The rock round here is good rock. Nobody climbs it. That's a crime.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: Summer. Best light for climbing. Worst light for selling coats.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: Rain. Everybody buys a rain shell and tells me about their knees.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: If you ever need someone to carry the other end of something heavy, I'm free after five.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: The tower's open? Is it as tall as it looks from the road? Taller? Don't tell me. Tell me.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: People are camping out there now. In tents. In the park. I'm jealous of strangers.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: Thanks for listening. Most people just tell me to go or stay.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: You make it look easy, out there. I know it isn't. That's why it's impressive.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: So you're the ranger. Good. Do you read? You look like someone who reads. Or someone who wants to.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: A question is a door. An answer is a wall. I prefer doors.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: The library closes Thursdays. Even books need a day with nobody looking at them.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: Rainy afternoons are for reading rooms. And for napping in them, quietly, with a book open.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: Morning. You're early. Early people find the best books. Late people find the funniest.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: The archive has a drawer for every year of the park. Some drawers are fuller than others.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: Autumn is the park's best season for reading about. Not for being in. Too many leaves.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: You opened the old cabin? There's a photograph of it in the archive. Same door. Different paint.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: Kettle Pond, open again. There's a poem about it in the local history section. It's not a good poem.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: You ask good questions. Keep asking them. I'll keep not answering them properly.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: I've worked here forty years. You're the first ranger to ask for the history section.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: A ranger! Ooh. Do you find things out there? Interesting things? Things people might want?

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: Everything in this shop is either a bargain or a treasure. Sometimes both. Never neither.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: Tuesdays I close and go bargain hunting. I always come back with something. Usually a teapot.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: Have you heard about Gus? No? Neither have I. Nothing ever happens to Gus. Terribly frustrating.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: Rain keeps the browsers in. Browsers are buyers who haven't admitted it yet.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: Winter. I sell candles by the crate. Everybody wants to look cozy.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: Evening. I do my sums. They come out different every time. It's very exciting.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: Visitors! In the park! Do they shop? Send them to me. Say Bev sent you. No, say you sent them.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: A badger? Making mischief? Oh, I'd pay to see that. I'd sell tickets.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: You've got good taste. For a person who lives in a hut.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: Between us, the best things in this shop aren't for sale. Don't tell the mayor.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Ranger.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Good wood's honest. Tells you where it wants to split.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Weekends I'm closed. I still come in. Just to look at things.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Rain. Wood swells. Wait a day.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Morning.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Planks, roofing, nails. Same price as the catalog. Same day.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Summer's for decks. Winter's for drawers. Spring's for fixing what winter did.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: The cabin door's back on. Good hinges, those. I know because I made them.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: You've been building. I can tell from your hands.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Thanks for stopping in.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Measure twice. Cut once. Talk... less than that.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Oh! The ranger. I paint the park. From photographs. I've never actually... it's a long story. It's a short story.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: The light by the creek in the afternoon is the closest I get to the forest. I'm working up to it.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Every painting I do of the park comes out a little different. I think the park's doing it.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Rain. I paint inside on rainy days. Mostly I watch the rain and call it research.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Autumn colours. Every year I run out of orange.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Afternoon. I've been sitting here an hour looking at one tree. It's going well.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: You opened the outlook? What does it look like from up there? Really look like?

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Somebody saw the pond's open. I've painted that pond four times. I've never seen it.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: You describe the park better than my photographs do. Keep talking.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Maybe one day I'll walk in with you. Not today. But one day. Probably.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: Welcome, welcome! Mayor Pruitt. Welcome to Humdrum, the most ordinary town in the region. We're very proud.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: Humdrum has won no awards. We're extremely consistent about it.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: Nothing happened here yesterday. Nothing is scheduled for tomorrow. Marvellous.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: The weather is entirely normal for the time of year. I checked.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: Rain! Ordinary rain. Wonderful.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: Weekends I'm at the bandstand, practising announcements. There's nothing to announce. Practice is important.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: Spring! The Thaw Fair is coming. It'll be exactly as nice as last year. I'm very excited.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: The park's having visitors? Ordinary people doing ordinary things. Splendid. Put it in the newsletter.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: A troll badger in the park? Well, that's a perfectly normal sort of badger to have.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: You're a credit to this town. And to ordinariness generally.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: I wrote you into this month's newsletter. 'Ranger continues to be fine.' Front page.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: Hello, ranger. I wondered when you'd come. Not in a mysterious way. You walk past here a lot.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: The cards say you'll have soup this week. The cards are very literal on Tuesdays.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: I open one evening a week. Which one? That's the fun.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: Rain is the sky being honest.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: Evening. My favourite. Things are clearer when there's less to see.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: Winter nights are long. Long nights are good for questions.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: The willow knows more than I do. It just won't say.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: You've been to the tower. I can tell. You're standing like someone who climbed stairs.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: You found people who were lost. That's the right kind of finding.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: You're learning to look sideways at things. Good. That's where most things are.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: Nothing I tell you is a secret. Some of it just takes a while to be true.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: Are you the RANGER? The real one? Have you seen Bigfoot? Have you seen ANYTHING? I'm Pip.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: Grandma says I can come to the square if I'm home before the lamps come on. They come on at dusk.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: I'm making a field guide. It has eleven pages. Ten are Bigfoot. One is a squirrel I wasn't sure about.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: Do rangers have to do homework? You should. It's only fair.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: It's raining! Footprints are easier to find in mud. That's science.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: Summer holidays! I'm going to be a junior ranger all summer. Starting now.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: When I grow up I'm going to be a ranger too. I'll have my own station. With a slide.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: Grandpa says the badger in the park is just a badger. Grandpa has never seen a badger, though.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: There are PEOPLE camping in the park now? Did they see anything? Can you ask them?

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: You're the best ranger I know. You're the only ranger I know. Still the best though.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: I drew you. You're taller in the drawing. It's a good drawing.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: Mondays everyone orders a double. Fridays everyone orders a treat. Wednesdays I sleep.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: If you see Gus, tell him his usual is ready. It's always ready. He always looks surprised.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: I named the espresso machine. I'm not telling you what. It knows.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: The square's quiet today. Quiet's my favourite flavour, after cinnamon.

rows.speaker: wren
rows.text: You've got sap on your sleeve. Badge of honour, around here.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: My mother's recipe, my grandmother's pot, my kitchen. Teo's apron. He'll grow into it.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: You want to know a secret? Extra lime. On everything. That's the secret.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: The mayor says Humdrum is ordinary. The mayor has never eaten my mole.

rows.speaker: rosa
rows.text: Sit down for once. The forest isn't going anywhere. I checked.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: Mom says I should talk to customers more. Hi. That's me talking to a customer.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: Have you ever had a song stuck in your head that you've never actually heard?

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: The square sounds different on market mornings. Busier. Like a rhythm section.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: I'm practising the guitar. Quietly. Very quietly. Basically just holding it.

rows.speaker: teo
rows.text: Wren says I'm a morning person who doesn't know it yet. I don't know it yet.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Socks matter more than boots. Nobody believes me until their third blister.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Nell reorganised the rope wall by colour. It's lovely. Nobody can find anything.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: I've climbed higher than anyone in this town. Mind you, it's a low town.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Bring a spare everything. Then a spare spare.

rows.speaker: marge
rows.text: Ask me about weather and I'll tell you what my knees say. They're never wrong.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: I've got a list of every peak within a day's drive. I've climbed none of them. Yet.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: Mom says Pelletiers don't sit still. She's been sitting on that stool for twenty years.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: The best view in town is from the outfitters' roof. Don't tell Mom I go up there.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: Wren's coffee could get you up a cliff. Or at least to the bottom of one.

rows.speaker: nell
rows.text: Sometimes I just walk the lane end to end. Twice. It's not much of a hike.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: Overdue books are like old friends. They come back when they're ready.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: Pip has read every book we have about Bigfoot. Twice. We have three.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: The quietest sound in the world is a library at closing time. I collect it.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: If you're looking for something, look one shelf to the left. It's always there.

rows.speaker: agnes
rows.text: The mayor borrowed a book on excitement once. Returned it unread. Very sensible of him.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: I've got a teapot shaped like a teapot. It's my most ordinary item. The mayor loves it.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: Everything's half price on Fridays. Everything's also double price on Thursdays. It evens out.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: Rosa says I talk too much. Rosa talks more than me. I counted.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: A ranger's hat would sell for a fortune in here. Just saying. Just mentioning it.

rows.speaker: bev
rows.text: I once sold a lamp to the same person three times. They kept giving it as a present.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Hm.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Oak's slow. Pine's quick. Both good.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Wren's coffee. Good.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Bring your hammer in sometime. I'll look at the handle.

rows.speaker: gus
rows.text: Nice weather for sanding.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: I mix a colour called Park Green. It's not quite right. It's never quite right.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Do you think trees know when they're being painted? They hold very still.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: I sold a painting of the lake to a tourist. I've never seen the lake. Neither had they.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Agnes says I should paint the town. I said the town is already painted. Badly. By Bev.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Every morning I put my boots by the door, just in case today's the day.

rows.speaker: sol
rows.text: Wren gives me free refills if I sketch her customers. I've drawn the mayor forty times.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: The town clock is exactly on time. I adjust it every morning to make sure.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: Our population is entirely steady. Nobody leaves. Nobody arrives. Except you. Welcome.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: I'm drafting a speech for the Thaw Fair. It's about the importance of thawing.

rows.speaker: lyle
rows.text: Humdrum's motto: Nothing To Report. I'm very proud of it. I wrote it.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: The moon was early last night. Not by much. It knows I noticed.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: Bring me a question sometime. The cards prefer questions to statements.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: Everyone in town has the same future: breakfast. After that it gets interesting.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: The creek runs both ways if you watch it long enough. Not really. But it's nice to think so.

rows.speaker: esme
rows.text: I knew you'd say hello. I'm glad you did anyway.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: Did you know a raccoon can open a jar? I can't. That's not fair.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: I'm practising tracking. I tracked Grandma to the kitchen. She was making soup.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: If you need a junior ranger I'm available after school and on Saturdays and also Sundays.

rows.speaker: pip
rows.text: My field guide has a new page. It's about you. It says 'tall, has a hat'.
